resources.string: Whitelister uses this service only while Instagram or Facebook is open. It reads their screen to recognise Reels, the Instagram Home feed and Explore, and, for the features you turn on, goes back or scrolls back to the top when you scroll them. Everything is processed on your device: nothing is stored or sent anywhere.
Whitelister needs Android\'s Accessibility Service (AccessibilityService API) to work. Please read how it is used.

While Instagram or Facebook is open, the content of their screen: the layout of the app, the view identifiers and the visible text, such as account names and captions. It does not read the content of any other app.

Only for the features you turn on: to recognise Reels, the Instagram Home feed and Explore, and to go back or scroll them back to the top when you scroll them. It also counts the minutes you spend on these screens each day, for the daily free time.

It is processed in memory, on your device, only at the moment the screen is shown. Nothing is recorded, stored or sent: Whitelister has no internet access, no analytics and no ads. The only things saved, on your device, are your settings and today\'s minutes per screen. You can turn the service off at any time in Android Settings › Accessibility.
Tap \"I agree\" to allow Whitelister to use the Accessibility Service as described here and in the Privacy Policy.

Last updated: 18 November 2026

Whitelister is an open-source Android app that helps you spend less time on Instagram and Facebook by blocking the endless-scroll features you choose to block. This policy explains what data the app accesses and what it does with it.

What data the app accesses
Whitelister uses Android's AccessibilityService API. While Instagram (com.instagram.android) or Facebook (com.facebook.katana) is on screen, the service reads that app's on-screen user interface: the view hierarchy, view identifiers, scroll positions and visible text such as account names and captions. The service is limited to these two apps and does not read the content of any other app; it only checks which app is in the foreground, to know when Instagram or Facebook is no longer on screen.

How the data is used
Only to provide the features you turn on:
• Remove Reels (Instagram and Facebook): recognise that you are watching a Reel and perform a back action when you swipe to another one.
• Block Feed (Instagram): recognise that the Home feed was scrolled below the Stories and scroll it back to the top, or tap the Home tab.
• Block Explore (Instagram): recognise that the Explore grid was scrolled and scroll it back to the top, or tap the Search tab.
• Daily free time: count the minutes you spend on each of these screens each day, so a block starts only after the free minutes you chose.
The screen content is processed in memory, on your device, at the moment it is shown. It is never recorded, stored or transmitted.

Data stored on your device
Only your feature settings (on/off and daily free minutes), whether you accepted the in-app accessibility disclosure, and, for each blockable screen, the minutes used today. These values stay in the app's private storage on your device and the minutes are replaced every day. If Android backup is turned on, Android may include these settings in your device backup, which is managed by Google under your backup settings, not by the developer.

Data collection and sharing
Whitelister collects no personal data and shares nothing with the developer or any third party. It has no internet permission, no analytics or crash-reporting SDKs, no ads and no account.

Retention and deletion
No data leaves your device, so the developer holds nothing to retain or delete. You can delete everything the app stored at any time by clearing its storage (Android Settings › Apps › Whitelister › Storage) or by uninstalling it.

Your controls
You can turn every feature off in the app and turn the accessibility service off at any time in Android Settings › Accessibility › Whitelister. The service does nothing until you accept the in-app disclosure.

Changes
Updates to this policy are published at github.com/mcap0/whitelister/blob/main/PRIVACY.md with a new date. If the app starts accessing data in a new way, you will be asked to accept the in-app disclosure again.

Contact
For questions about this policy, open an issue at github.com/mcap0/whitelister/issues.

Whitelister is an independent project and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Instagram, Facebook or Meta.
